options.text: The canal bank and the hillside have different conditions, so different plants live there.
Different regions always have different plants, even when their conditions are the same.
The hillside is dry and rocky because cactus grows there.
No kind of plant can live on both a wet canal bank and a dry rocky hillside.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem:
Ojas compares reeds growing along a wet canal bank with cactus on a dry rocky hillside.

Why do the plants in the two regions differ?

part_answers.answer: Plants differ across regions because conditions such as water and soil dryness differ.

teacher.key_rationale: Plants differ across regions because conditions differ. Regions need not differ when conditions match; cactus does not cause the hillside climate; some plants can live in more than one kind of place.
